subject: Organizing a project or repository into one canonical, version-controlled structure: choose the owning repo and path,…

evals.prompt: Define canonical-repo-structure in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the canonical-repo-structure skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind canonical-repo-structure. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "should I rebase or merge this feature branch?". Should canonical-repo-structure activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force canonical-repo-structure onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to taxonomy-design, skill-infrastructure, semantics, information-architecture, version-control, doc-updater, refactor, naming-conventions.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "organize this repo so every script and command has one canonical home". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying canonical-repo-structure.

Place canonical-repo-structure among its adjacent skills (taxonomy-design, skill-infrastructure, semantics, information-architecture, version-control, doc-updater, refactor, naming-conventions). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about canonical-repo-structure and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
